key_insight: Iterative refinement—repeatedly verifying and correcting generated images against decomposed prompt constraints—substantially improves alignment on richly compositional text-to-image prompts. This yields more accurate multi-object, relation, and attribute satisfaction than single-pass sampling or naive step increases.
problem_solved: Text-to-image models fail to reliably render complex, compositional prompts that require simultaneously satisfying many objects, relations, and attributes; existing inference tricks (more denoising steps or parallel sampling) are insufficient for such multi-constraint scenarios.
method: Decompose complex prompts into smaller constraints (objects, relations, attributes) and use a looped inference procedure that verifies which constraints are unmet.
Apply targeted iterative edits or re-sampling steps guided by a verifier or internal reasoning signal (inspired by chain-of-thought) to progressively satisfy remaining constraints.
Stop when a verifier indicates prompt alignment or after a fixed budget of refinement steps, producing higher-fidelity, compositionally correct images.
impact: Enables practitioners to get more reliable, faithful image outputs for complex prompts without retraining models—useful for design, illustration, and downstream evaluation tasks that demand precise compositional control.

paper_title: Iterative Refinement Improves Compositional Image Generation
paper_authors: Shantanu Jaiswal, Mihir Prabhudesai, Nikash Bhardwaj, Zheyang Qin, Amir Zadeh
